name: State of Florida
policy_note: Structural research pointer only. NO substantive statutory rules — student packets are facts-only; finding the controlling law is the exercise. Chapter-level locators are navigational aids. Instructor notes may cite specifics, verified at publish.

circuit_court.name: Florida Circuit Court
circuit_court.note: Trial court of general jurisdiction, organized into 20 judicial circuits by county. Handles higher-value civil (incl. the m13 auto-negligence jury trial), felony criminal, family, and probate matters. Probate is heard in the Probate Division of the Circuit Court.

intermediate_appellate.name: Florida District Court of Appeal
intermediate_appellate.note: Intermediate appellate court, organized into six districts.

specialty_divisions.probate: Probate Division of the Circuit Court — estate administration and will contests; captioned 'In re Estate of <Decedent>.'

shape_specific_notes.auto_negligence: Florida negligence practice involves distinctive doctrines students should research (e.g., the state's comparative-fault approach and no-fault/PIP motor-vehicle insurance framework). Civil jury trial in the Circuit Court. Students research the current standard themselves.
shape_specific_notes.wills_probate: Florida's constitutional and statutory HOMESTEAD protections sharply constrain how a homestead may be devised and shield it from creditors — the deliberate teaching hook for the m20 probate contest. Students research the current homestead-devise restrictions themselves.

navigational_code_areas: Negligence / damages and comparative fault: Fla. Stat. ch. 768 — a starting point for m13.
Wills, probate, and homestead devise: Fla. Stat. chs. 732 and 733, plus Art. X, § 4, Fla. Const. — a starting point for m20.

disclaimer: Structural/navigational reference only, current as of 2026. Verify all law against the official sources above; nothing here is legal advice.
